name: Fortive Corporation

profile.description: Fortive Corporation is an industrial technology company providing essential instruments, software, and services through two segments: Intelligent Operating Solutions (Fluke, Accruent, Gordian, ServiceChannel — Q3 2026 revenue $767M, +9.1% core) and Advanced Healthcare Solutions (ASP sterilization, Censis, Provation — Q3 revenue $340M, +3.1% core). Q3 2026 revenue was $1.11B (+7.8% reported, +7.2% core) with adjusted EPS of $0.77 (+13%), and management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $3.10-$3.14 (~15% growth). Spun off from Danaher in 2016, Fortive completed the Ralliant (Precision Technologies) separation in June 2025, when Olumide Soroye succeeded Jim Lico as CEO; the 'new Fortive' has ~10,000 employees and has repurchased ~13% of its shares since the separation.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Since its 2016 Danaher spin, Fortive has reshaped itself twice — spinning Vontier (2020) and Ralliant (June 2025) — while buying Accruent, Gordian, ServiceChannel and Provation to pivot toward software-enabled, recurring-revenue workflow solutions, a significant repositioning that opened new revenue streams [3]. AI Deployment (1/2): CEO Soroye says Fortive has run an AI Center of Excellence since 2017 and that engineers are ~20% more productive using AI coding assistants, but no AI product revenue or dollar savings have been disclosed [3]. Market Share (2/2): Fluke remains the global leader in handheld electrical test tools and ASP is a leading hospital sterilization franchise, with IOS posting 9.1% core growth in Q3 2026 [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management cites ongoing new product introductions and software innovation under the Fortive Accelerated plan, but no named next-gen launches with revenue targets [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of $342M was ~6.7% of reported revenue, above typical diversified-industrial levels [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Fortive's purpose — providing 'essential technology for the people who accelerate progress' — is clear about whom it serves, and its 2026 proxy ties sustainability to that 'shared purpose,' but the statement is not distinctive and a 10-year-old, twice-reshaped company has not validated it through decades of execution [4]. Community Impact (1/2): Fortive runs standard corporate responsibility programs and SBTi-aligned emissions targets documented in its sustainability reporting, without distinctive, dollar-quantified community investment found [4][5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found; the workforce shrank from ~18,000 to ~10,000 with the Ralliant separation, so no evidence of above-average retention can be credited. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider statistics show zero open-market purchases and five insider sales across Q4 2025-Q3 2026, i.e., net selling [6].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored for the Growth sleeve. D/E of 60% (target <=70%) and forward P/E of 19.7x (target <=20) both score full marks, and the 14.8% TTM net margin approaches the 20% target [6][7]. ROE of 10.6% (2x weight) sits below the 15% target, reflecting $6B+ of acquisition goodwill (tangible book is negative), and the 5-year revenue CAGR of ~3.1% (2x weight) is derived from restated continuing-operations revenue ($3.91B in 2023 to $4.16B in 2025), because Vontier and Ralliant spins make reported history non-comparable. Forward PEG of 1.83 (FMP; Yahoo shows 0.98) scores mid-range; Q3 revenue grew 7.8% YoY with TTM FCF of $1.06B [1]. Liquidity floor cleared easily: ~2.35M shares x $65.23 = ~$153M daily.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Fluke's test and measurement tools and ASP's FDA-regulated sterilization systems perform physical-world work that AI cannot substitute, and no analyst commentary found flags AI displacement risk for Fortive's lines [1][3]. The software franchises (Accruent, Gordian, ServiceChannel, Provation) have deep workflow integration and proprietary cost data (Gordian's RSMeans) but face moderate long-run exposure to AI-native facilities and procurement tools, which keeps the score in the PROTECTED band rather than IMMUNE. AI Opportunity (0/1): Soroye frames AI as a productivity multiplier ('make a team of 10,000 feel like 100,000') with 20% engineering productivity gains, but Fortive discloses no quantified AI-driven revenue [3].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Fortive is a disciplined operator more than a cause-driven institution. The Fortive Business System gives it a durable continuous-improvement culture and leadership has shown willingness to reshape the portfolio repeatedly, but the repeated spins and buybacks (~$2.3B, 13% of shares since the Ralliant separation) look more like portfolio optimization than pursuit of a Just Cause, and the company has yet to prove a purpose that outlasts its leaders.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Essential technology for the people who accelerate progress' is a reasonable statement but reads as a corporate mission rather than a Just Cause people sacrifice for [4]. The cause has not been tested over decades — the company has been reconstituted three times in ten years — and strategic moves trace more to margin and recurring-revenue optimization than to an idealistic future state.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The FBS provides a shared operating language and Lico's planned handoff to Soroye in June 2025 preserved continuity [3]. No evidence of exceptional psychological safety or retention was found, and the workforce has been split repeatedly through spinoffs, so trust is judged adequate rather than exceptional.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Fortive's language centers on continuous improvement via FBS and customer productivity rather than crushing competitors, and its operating model openly borrows from Danaher, a rival it treats as a benchmark [3][4].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The Vontier (2020) and Ralliant (2025) separations fundamentally changed Fortive's revenue mix toward software and healthcare workflow [3]. However, these were portfolio carve-outs executed with the same FBS acquisition playbook, not a Just-Cause-driven reinvention of the core business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership chose to shed large, profitable instrument businesses (Tektronix and sensing moved to Ralliant) to concentrate on higher-quality recurring revenue, accepting a smaller company [3]. Heavy repurchases (~$300M in Q3 2026 alone) and a reduced post-spin dividend show capital allocation conviction but also a shareholder-return emphasis Sinek would view cautiously [1].

investment_thesis: Fortive's 'new Fortive' is accelerating: Q3 2026 revenue rose 7.8% to $1.11B (7.2% core) with adjusted EPS up 13% to $0.77, IOS grew 9.1% core at a 35.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, and management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $3.10-$3.14, ~15% growth [1]. TTM free cash flow of $1.06B (~5.5% FCF yield on a $19.4B market cap) funds aggressive buybacks — ~$2.3B, or ~13% of shares, since the Ralliant separation — while D/E stays a manageable ~60% [1][6]. At ~19.7x forward earnings, the stock trades in line with industrial-technology peers despite a 63% gross margin and growing recurring software mix.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on growth quality and returns on capital. Advanced Healthcare Solutions grew just 3.1% core in Q3, and the restated continuing-operations revenue base grew only ~3% annually from 2023 to 2025, so the acceleration must persist to justify the multiple [1][2]. ROE of 10.6% and negative tangible book value reflect more than $6B of acquisition goodwill, and insiders have been net sellers with no open-market purchases in the past year [6]. The Inspire Impact Score of -49 (MISALIGNED, LGBT Activism) limits suitability for faith-based mandates.
key_catalysts: Core growth acceleration: IOS core growth of 9.1% in Q3 2026 and raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.10-$3.14 (~15% growth) could drive estimate revisions into 2027 [1]
Capital return: ~$300M of Q3 buybacks (~2% of diluted shares) and $1.06B TTM FCF support continued double-digit EPS growth even with mid-single-digit revenue growth [1]
AI-enabled productivity under CEO Soroye — 20% engineering productivity gains from AI tools — could expand margins across Fluke, Accruent and Gordian software [3]
key_risks: Healthcare softness: AHS core growth of only 3.1% and an 11.2% GAAP operating margin in Q3 2026 could weigh on the consolidated growth story if hospital capital budgets tighten [1]
Acquisition-heavy balance sheet: negative tangible book value and 10.6% ROE mean any impairment or poor integration of software acquisitions would hit returns [6]
Software exposure to AI-native competitors in facilities maintenance (ServiceChannel) and construction cost data (Gordian) could erode pricing over time
